observationsNotFindings: The draft's exhaustive leftover statement and its illustrative one are in different places. Line 99 gives the exact open set, leftoverDesign remains [OBL-G30-FX-AUTHORING], and that is the claim I checked against join.v3's obligation table. Decision item 2 separately names three closed obligations by hand and does not name the other two closed ones, OBL-G30-EXECUTION and OBL-EE7ABD-UNNAMED-REMAINDER-CLOSED. Because the exact claim is stated exhaustively elsewhere, the hand list reads as illustration rather than as an enumeration that has gone short, and I did not charge it.

The measured-inputs table cites seven rows but the lineage prose leans on three artifacts the table does not pin: g30-leftover-join.v3, and the two D-158 turn-2 verdict files. I recomputed all three from v2's recordedInputs rather than trusting the prose, and all three matched. The load-bearing pins are therefore reachable, but they are reachable one hop away through v2 rather than directly from the draft's own table.

v2 carries both a file08CarriesG30 key and a file08DoesNotCarryG30 key. They read true and false, so they are complementary and the file is self-consistent, but the pair is an unusual shape for a boundary assertion and would be a live contradiction risk if a future revision updated only one of them.

The frozen-v1 row in the measured-inputs table does more work than a digest row usually does: it carries the historical HEAD and the historical required-now inline in its label cell. That is what makes the v1-is-not-current attack hard to land from the table alone, and it is a good pattern, but it means a reader who scans only digest columns will miss the disclaimer.

The v1 leftoverNameNote is not at v1's top level; it sits at whatThisCloses.leftoverNameNote. A reviewer who probes only top-level keys gets null and could wrongly conclude the draft invented the note. I walked the whole tree before forming a view on that attack line.

v1 has a claude2 independent review on disk and no codex counterpart, while v2 has both. The draft's sentence 'Dual independent ACCEPT 0/0 now exists' is doing real work: it is the substantive difference between the frozen predecessor and this subject, not a restatement of the same standing at a new version number.

The repeated 'Does not invent a D9 code.' at header lines 26 and 39 is present in adopted D-229 at the same two positions. It reads as duplication on a first pass, so I checked the precedent before deciding whether it was a drafting slip. It is house pattern, and changing it here would make this entry deviate from the branch rather than tidy it.
